title: UIAA Medical Commission Factsheet on Altitude Sickness
publisher: International Climbing and Mountaineering Federation (UIAA) Medical Commission
claims: Above about 2700 m, a reasonable recommendation is not to climb more than 400 m above the previous night's sleeping altitude.
A rest day after every two days of altitude gain may help; climbing high and sleeping low may support acclimatisation.
Physical fitness does not protect against altitude sickness, and very fit people may push harder and increase risk.
Alcohol and sleeping pills can depress breathing and interfere with acclimatisation; excessive exertion is a risk factor.
For people flying directly to high altitude without time to acclimatise, prophylactic acetazolamide may make sense if there is no allergy history.
